chapter: Hearing Louis and the Baton Rouge scene
title: Second lines, band funerals and Giddis in Baton Rouge
summary: Baton Rouge had second-line parades, bands every few days, and funerals with music, and Joe mentions the Giddis undertaking family.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Did they do second line in Baton Rouge like they do in New Orleans?

See, the world(?) over followed music. In Baton Rouge, two... You heard a band on the average of two or three times a week, a small town, as small as it was. They'd usually be advertising a dance or playing a funeral or something.
Did they have funerals in Baton Rouge?

Oh, that was one of the big things. And they had a cemetery not far from my house, you see. Now, Giddis... Giddis had an undertaking parlor; that same Giddis and Morse in New Orleans that had that undertaking parlor with that big eye in front of it at one time, that would look at you...
Gertrude Giddis or someone like that...
Ginny Giddis was her name. They called them Giddis and Morse. They were partners.
Giddis and Morse, I remember, yeah.
